text:
alice-support: FYI customer (acme) reporting OAuth logins failing for both GitHub and Google. They reach our callback but get invalid_state / 403 during token exchange. Happens intermittently behind their CDN. Repro steps attached.
sam-frontend: can you paste the full callback URL (redact codes)? curious if state is missing/truncated.
alice-support: pasted (redacted):
https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback?code=REDACTED&state=eyJhbGci...%3D&scope=openid
also another example where state appears twice (weird):
https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback?state=XYZ123&code=REDACTED&state=XYZ123%3D...
sam-frontend: whoa, state twice. browsers will keep first or last depending on parsing; our handler expects the single state cookie we set earlier so mismatch.
devops: do we have any proxy/CDN in front that might be appending querystring? common bug: proxy configured to forward original args plus backend args, ending up with duplicate params.
alice-support: customer says they run Fastly + an internal nginx which does a rewrite for path normalization.
tyler-sre: quick theory: nginx rule was doing something like `proxy_pass http://app-backend$request_uri;` while also configured backend_location with `?state=$arg_state` causing double-append. Result: request arrives with two state params: `state=abc&...&state=abc%3D` where one is URL-encoded chunk. Our server reads the last param (framework picks last) but the state cookie contains the first => invalid state.
sam-frontend: logs show token exchange 403s at 2026-11-02T14:03:12Z spike. I pulled raw request from the customer's frontend logs and it matches the duplicated param pattern.
alice-support: customer provided a curl repro we ran internally:
```
curl -v "https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback?state=abc123&code=xyz789&state=abc123%3D" -b "_session_state=abc123"
```
response: 403 invalid_state
tyler-sre: mitigation options:
- quick backend tweak: accept first state param parsed instead of last (cheap patch) OR
- change callback handler to canonicalize state = decodeURIComponent(first) and compare to cookie
- immediate customer-side suggestion: bypass the nginx rewrite (temporary) or upgrade Fastly config to not append original query params
longer term: fix proxy config so it doesn't append querystring twice. Example nginx anti-pattern that caused it:
```
location /oauth/callback {
  rewrite ^/oauth/callback(.*) /oauth/callback$1?state=$arg_state? break;
  proxy_pass http://app-backend$request_uri;
}
```
Instead do not explicitly append `?state=...` or use `proxy_pass http://app-backend$uri$is_args$args;` so args are handled only once.
devops: on our side, we can push a 30m hotfix to prefer the first state param. I'll open PR and a canary deploy to prod. Also will add extra logging for duplicate params so we can measure impact.
oauth-bot: alert: oauth_invalid_state rate +320% (14:00-14:10 UTC). customer ticket #SUP-4421 linked.
alice-support: thanks. I've told the customer we have a mitigation and a patch plan. I'll coordinate a short maintenance window for the nginx change if they want us to manage it. :thumbsup:
sam-frontend: file PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1123 — adds tolerant state check and extra logging.
tyler-sre: after deploy, we should verify with customer's repro curl and ask them to test from their CDN edge.
alice-support: noted, passing to acme to test once we deploy. closing loop in ticket when verified. :white_check_mark:
